summary: Split batch job caused partial enterprise discount not applied across multi-run invoice
description:
Issue summary: Customer QuantaDocs reports that an enterprise tier discount for bulk embedding jobs was applied to only a subset of micro-batch runs, resulting in a higher-than-expected invoice line for the most recent billing cycle.
Impact: Customer saw a $1,200 unexpected charge and is asking for credit and explanation. This impacts billing accuracy and trust for enterprise reserved pricing.
Environment: Production, mixed-region batch processing: primary routing to us-east but overflow to eu-west during a dense overnight window. Model: embedder-quant-v2 (quantized variant).
Requested: confirmation whether discount should have applied across the entire logical job, provisional credit while we investigate, and corrective invoice if needed.
steps_to_reproduce: Customer ran a single logical batch job split into 48 micro-runs over a 3-hour window starting 2026-02-26T23:10:00Z.
Routing policy overflowed ~12 micro-runs to eu-west due to temporary us-east saturation (dedicated fallback to hosted for overflow).
Billing system receives postbacks from both regions; postbacks were assigned different pricing tags (enterprise_discount_tag and hosted_fallback_tag) depending on routing path.
Invoice generation aggregated lines by tag and region; enterprise discount appears on us-east lines only.
Customer observed invoice lines: discounted_us-east: $3,800, undisc_eu-west: $1,200 (expected all discounted).
logs: postback-log snippets: POST /v1/postback status 200 for run_id 9f1a (us-east) tag enterprise_discount_tag
postback-log: POST /v1/postback status 200 for run_id b7c3 (eu-west) tag hosted_fallback_tag
billing-aggregator: matched 35 postbacks to enterprise contract id QD-ENT-23, 13 postbacks matched fallback tariff FK-STD-01
router-trace: 2026-02-27T00:02:14Z overflow triggered due to GPU pool saturation - fallback executed
comments: 2026-03-10 Maya Chen (customer): We expected our enterprise bulk-embed discount to apply across the whole job. Please advise why some micro-runs were billed at the hosted fallback rate.

2026-03-10 Arjun Patel (Support): Thanks Maya — we're pulling the postback traces and contract mapping. Can you confirm whether the job was created with the org-level pin to the enterprise contract (contract_id QD-ENT-23)?
2026-03-10 Maya Chen (customer): Yes, job was initiated under org-id quanta-main, contract id QD-ENT-23. We verified the API key had enterprise tags in the Console at start time.

2026-03-11 Billing Eng (Lena Ortiz): Initial analysis: aggregator assigned fallback tariff for postbacks that arrived with routing metadata region=eu-west and route=fallback-hosted. Need to confirm whether contract mapping should supersede route-based tariff assignment.

2026-03-11 SRE (Derek Nguyen): Router trace confirms overflow window due to transient GPU shortage. Postbacks were delivered from eu-west edge proxies with tag hosted_fallback_tag. Proposing to re-run aggregator match logic to prefer contract bindings over route tag.

2026-03-12 Arjun Patel (Support): Actioned provisional credit of $1,200 pending reconciliation (customer notified). Running backfill to remap tariff tags by org-contract ID and will re-generate invoice if backfill adjusts lines.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Postback->tariff assignment used route tag precedence over contract binding, causing fallback postbacks to miss enterprise discount mapping.
Hypothesis 2: Edge proxy in eu-west sanitized or rewrote contract_id header for overflowed postbacks under high load, resulting in aggregator mismatch.

Findings: Aggregator logs show 13 postbacks for this logical job lacked contract_id metadata at billing time; header parsing component logged 'missing-org-header' at 2026-02-27T00:05:12Z for proxy b-eu-4.
Correlated with PR 482 which changed postback normalization to rename header X-Org-Id -> X-Org (deployed 2026-02-25). Some proxies still emit X-Org-Id which caused downstream mismatch.
Impact: Missing contract binding caused tariff fallback for ~12.5% of micro-runs resulting in $1,200 delta.
Temporary mitigation: credit issued; long-term fix requires postback normalization patch and aggregation re-run for affected billing window.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-12: Provisional credit of $1,200 applied to QuantaDocs account pending invoice re-issue. Finance ticket created to hold charge reversal while corrected invoice is finalized.

Technical fix: Rollback normalization mismatch introduced in PR 482 and deploy a compatibility shim that accepts both X-Org-Id and X-Org headers. Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood/usage-postbacks/pull/495

Data fix: Re-run postback aggregator for billing window 2026-02-26T23:00:00Z -> 2026-02-27T02:00:00Z with updated header acceptance rules. This will remap 13 postbacks to enterprise contract and re-calc invoice lines.
Follow-ups: Add an end-to-end test for header normalization and a monitoring alert when >1% of postbacks arrive without contract_id metadata. Owner: Billing Eng (Lena Ortiz). Due: 2026-03-19.
Customer communication: Notified Maya on 2026-03-12 that provisional credit posted and we will follow up with final invoice by 2026-03-15.
